title: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical Variation
line: The bishop comes out with a hit on the knight, and Black keeps it safe from White's h-pawn.

steps.text: The Caro-Kann: Black's center pawn hits e4, and White guards it with a knight.
Black takes, the bishop comes out to hit the knight, and the knight hits it back.
Step back to g6. The bishop stays outside your pawns.
steps.after: White's pawn on the edge runs up to chase the bishop.

steps.text: Push the pawn on h7 one square. If White's pawn comes to h5, your bishop can step back to h7.

wrong.g8f6: Then White's pawn comes to h5, and your bishop is short of squares.

steps.text: Bring the knight to d7. It keeps White's knight out of e5.

wrong.g6f5: The knight on g3 takes it.

steps.text: Trade bishops. White usually takes back with the queen, which comes out early.
Push the pawn on e7 one square. Now your other bishop can come out.
steps.after: Your bishop got out and was traded, and your pawns make a solid wall on the light squares.

summary: In the Classical, the bishop comes out early, steps back when chased and is traded before the pawns close it in.
